title: 1987 AHSME Problem 6
statement: In the \(\triangle ABC\) shown, \(D\) is some interior point, and \(x,\) \(y,\) \(z,\) \(w\) are the measures of angles in degrees. Solve for \(x\) in terms of \(y,\) \(z,\) and \(w.\)

solutions.text:
Let the unlabelled angles of triangle \(ADB\) at \(A\) and \(B\) be \(\alpha\) and \(\beta.\) Then \[ \alpha+\beta+w=180^\circ. \] The angle sum of triangle \(ABC\) gives \[ (\alpha+y)+(\beta+z)+x=180^\circ. \] Subtracting yields \(x+y+z=w,\) so \(x=w-y-z.\)

Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: Name the two unlabelled angles at \(A\) and \(B\) inside triangle \(ADB\)
Subtract the angle sum of \(\triangle ADB\) from that of \(\triangle ABC\)
